stage_name: S6 "Authorization and physical presence" -- basic slice: capability taxonomy (#18), central authentication/authorization middleware (#19) wired into a real registration-level dispatch wrapper, non-leaky stable 401/403 errors (#23), and the login/logout/session subset of #17 (POST /api/v1/auth/login, POST /api/v1/auth/logout, GET /api/v1/auth/session) -- and, as a consequence, the FIRST-EVER production registration of the /api/v1 contract (plan S4 #28/#29's "S6 owns the first production registration path")
note_on_commits: No new commit created; commits are only made on explicit user request. Builds on the prior HIL session's work (already committed via PR #51/#53, merged to canary) and the security_bounds.cpp CI fix from the same session.
sequencing_note: User chose this cluster ("Authorization and physical presence", #18-23) after the prior HIL session closed out the reachable half of "HTTPS and sessions" (#7-17 minus #12/#17, both blocked here). Recon before designing anything found that #19's middleware has nothing to authenticate a caller AGAINST without a login route (#17, nominally a different cluster) -- so this sub-slice's scope was explicitly widened, with the user's confirmation, to cover #17's login/logout/session routes together with #18/#19/#23. The remaining #17 routes (provisioning/enroll, auth/password, certificate rotation, factory-reset) and #20-22 (the physical-presence grant itself, needing a not-yet-built GPIO/button HAL) are deliberately NOT built here -- named as the next sub-slice.

design_decisions.decision: Capability is a single, flat 9-value taxonomy (plan #18's exact list) with no per-user grant table -- every authenticated session holds every capability the current build supports.
design_decisions.why: This codebase has exactly one administrative role (a single AdminVerifierRecord, S6 'Provisioning and credentials' #5) -- there is no user/role concept anywhere to check a real subset against. Building a fake per-capability check would verify nothing real, the same reasoning gateway_identity_verification.hpp's own header already applies to its narrower self-consistency-vs-uniqueness scoping decision. capability.hpp documents this explicitly and names what WOULD need to change (only the grant step) if a real multi-role system is ever added. The per-route Capability tag passed at every v1 handler's registration call site is real today for two things: filtering GET /api/v1/auth/session's 'actor capabilities' response by actual build capability (ota/rcp availability), and a self-describing, grep-able label for the not-yet-built #30/#31 audit-record 'action' field.

design_decisions.decision: The middleware is a registration-level dispatch WRAPPER (web_route_auth_dispatch.cpp's register_authenticated_uri_handler_v1() + authenticated_dispatch_trampoline), not an inline check added to the top of each of the 13 pre-existing v1 handler function bodies.
design_decisions.why: Every pre-existing v1 handler's own host test calls that handler function directly (e.g. devices_get_handler_v1(&req)), never through a real dispatch path -- that is how this project's v1 handlers have been host-testable without a real esp_http_server at all. An inline auth check would have forced every one of those tests to first fabricate a valid session, conflating business-logic testing with authentication testing. Wrapping only the REGISTRATION call means existing handler bodies and their existing tests are unchanged byte-for-byte, the real (only reachable-by-a-client) dispatch path is fully gated, and the wrapper gets its own small, focused test suite (test_web_handlers_auth.cpp) instead of duplicating auth setup across every handler's tests.

design_decisions.decision: Login's own response never includes the CSRF token; only GET /api/v1/auth/session does.
design_decisions.why: Plan #14's exact text: 'CSRF token is a separate 256-bit session-bound value returned only by the authenticated session endpoint.' Read literally rather than assumed -- the client's flow is login (sets cookie) -> GET /auth/session (reads CSRF token + capabilities).

design_decisions.decision: Logout is mutation-grade (requires CSRF+Origin, same as any other state-changing route), even though the plan does not name an exception for it.
design_decisions.why: Plan #15's text ('every state-changing browser request') names no logout exception; a forged-logout CSRF attack is lower-impact than a forged-mutation one, but inventing an unstated exception would be a real, undocumented judgment call in the wrong direction (weakening a plan requirement, not narrowing an ambiguous one).

design_decisions.decision: register_web_routes_v1() is now actually called (from web_server.cpp's start_production_https() path only, never development) -- the first production registration of the /api/v1 contract, previously forbidden by plan S4 #28/#29 until 'S6 owns the first production registration path'.
design_decisions.why: INV-H010 (check_arch_invariants.sh) was re-read before changing anything: its check_absent guard name-greps main/app_main.cpp specifically, never components/web_ui/web_server.cpp (the real composition root) -- confirming the invariant was always scoped to block the WRONG place from doing this, not to block it everywhere. web_server.cpp's start_production_https() is exactly 'the production listener/control-plane composition root' the plan's own prose (just above the #18 heading) describes registering mutation routes from 'only after certificate/trust validation, secure-storage readiness and central authentication/authorization policy initialization' -- this sub-slice's own auth plumbing is that last precondition. No invariant-script change was needed or made; re-verified via a real check_arch_invariants.sh run (still high=0/medium=0/low=0).

design_decisions.decision: v1/auth routes are registered in production only, never development.
design_decisions.why: The session cookie carries the `Secure` attribute (plan #14) -- meaningless (browsers will not send it back) without HTTPS, which only the production listener serves (S6 #7). Development is completely unchanged by this sub-slice.

real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.defect: New test_web_handlers_auth.cpp segfaulted (ASan: 'member access within misaligned address ... which requires 8 byte alignment').
real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.root_cause: Test bug, not a production bug: for a WRAPPED route (session/logout), a real esp_http_server dispatch places register_authenticated_uri_handler_v1()'s own AuthenticatedRouteBinding* in req->user_ctx (that is the whole point of the wrapper), never the WebRouteContext* directly. The test initially set req.user_ctx to an unrelated pointer, which the trampoline then mis-cast as a binding.
real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.fix: Set req.user_ctx to the CAPTURED registration's own .user_ctx (i.e. exactly what a real dispatch would place there) for every wrapped-route test case. Confirmed via a full ASan+UBSan rebuild after the fix: clean.

real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.defect: auth_logout_post_handler_v1's clear_header[64] buffer was too small for build_session_cookie_clear_header()'s real output ('zgw_session=; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1; Max-Age=0' = 72 chars + NUL = 73 bytes needed) -- build_session_cookie_clear_header() correctly detected the truncation and returned false, so the real bug (undersized buffer) surfaced as a genuine handler failure (logout returning ESP_FAIL), not a silent truncation.
real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.root_cause: Estimated the buffer size instead of computing it from the real format string.
real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.fix: clear_header[64] -> clear_header[96]. Confirmed by the same test case (logout with correct CSRF+Origin) now returning ESP_OK and a correctly truncation-free Set-Cookie header.

real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.defect: Real ESP-IDF target build failure: 'httpd_handler_t' does not name a type on ESP_PLATFORM.
real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.root_cause: httpd_handler_t is a name this project's OWN host mock invents (web_handler_common.hpp); the real esp_http_server.h declares httpd_uri_t::handler inline (`esp_err_t (*handler)(httpd_req_t *r)`) with no portable named typedef at all. AuthenticatedRouteBinding's real_handler field used httpd_handler_t, compiling fine on host (where the name exists) but not on the real target.
real_defects_found_and_fixed_this_sub_sl.fix: decltype(httpd_uri_t{}.handler) instead of naming a type -- portable across both host and ESP_PLATFORM by construction, confirmed by a full real idf.py build succeeding after the fix (both dev and ZGW_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1 profiles).

honest_scope_boundary: No external HTTP client / real hardware exercise of these routes this round (no new HIL session) -- verification depth is host-test + real-target compile/link, matching every other S6 sub-slice's own accepted bar before HIL became possible, and matching plan #7's own precedent (compile+link accepted since this sandbox has no way to observe a live TLS handshake).

GET /api/v1/auth/session's CSRF token is delivered in the JSON response body, not a separate header or a double-submit-cookie pattern -- a real judgment call (plan #14 names only 'returned... by the authenticated session endpoint', not a transport). Documented at the call site, not hidden.

No rate limiting on POST /api/v1/auth/login yet (plan #28, cluster 'Rate limiting and audit', not started) -- a real, present brute-force exposure until that cluster lands. Named directly rather than left implicit.

No audit logging of login/logout/denied-authorization events yet (plan #30/#31, same not-yet-started cluster) -- capability_token() already produces the exact action label that future work will want, but nothing writes an audit record today.

#17's remaining routes (provisioning/enroll, auth/password, certificate rotation, factory-reset) and #20-22 (the physical-presence grant itself) are not built -- all need a physical GPIO/button HAL that does not exist in this repository yet. This is the natural next sub-slice, and (per the prior HIL session) could now genuinely be hardware-in-the-loop tested on the connected ESP32-C6, unlike everything in this sub-slice.
